articles.title: Sequoia and Greenoaks lead massive $5BN Series C funding round in Isomorphic Labs
Isomorphic Labs raises $5bn backed by Sequoia and A16z
AI drug discovery giant Isomorphic Labs raises €4.5 billion in blockbuster funding round

Isomorphic Labs raises $5B series C months after $2.1B round
Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion as AI drug developer targets clinical trials

brief.essentiel: Isomorphic Labs , an AI company focussed on designing and developing new medicines, today announced a €4.5 billion ($5 billion) Series C financing round to accelerate the scientific breakthroughs and proprietary AI advances.
points: Demis Hassabis’'s Isomorphic Labs has raised a massive $5bn Series C funding round, just six months after raising $2.1bn in a Series B funding, as it looks to leverage AI to power a new generation of medicines.

The new funding round was co-led by California-based VCs Greenoaks and Sequoia, with Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive Capital, Alphabet, Alphabet’s GV and CapitalG, Temasek, and the Sovereign AI fund also participating.

In the UK, London-based Helical raised €8.4 million for its virtual AI laboratory, Ternary Therapeutics secured €4.1 million for AI-designed molecular glues, and Sable Bio attracted €3.15 million for its drug-safety platform.
Elsewhere, France’s Orakl Oncology raised €30 million and Rivercell secured €22 million, while Switzerland’s Adaptyv Bio announced €34.35 million for automated biological testing.

points: The round was co-led by General Atlantic and QED Investors , with participation from Evolution Equity Partners, Airtree, Forestay Capital, Y Combinator, FT Partners, Latitude, Inception Fund and 13Books Capital, bringing the company's total funding to $350 million.
This brings Model ML’s total funding to €318 million ($350 million), following a €68 million ($75 million) Series A in November 2025 .

In the UK, London-based 9fin raised €148 million for its debt-markets intelligence platform, while Nevis secured €62 million for AI-driven wealth management workflows and Stacks raised €19 million for enterprise finance automation.
Elsewhere, Berlin-based Moss closed €30 million to expand its Finance AI suite, and Copenhagen’s Performativ secured €11.96 million for wealth management software.

articles.title: Fermat raises $8M to bridge the gap between fashion designers and manufacturers
Barcelona-based Fermat raises €7.26 million for its AI operating system for fashion and luxury brands

brief.essentiel: Fermat , the Barcelona-based AI platform for the fashion industry, has raised $8 million in seed funding to open a New York office and expand its software from a design tool to full garment production.
points: Seventeen major fashion companies plan to invest a combined $40.9 billion in technology, stores and supply chains in 2026, up 12.5 per cent on 2025, according to S&P data reported by Modaes, with AI and supply-chain digitalisation among their priorities.
Kibo Ventures and Lunar Ventures lead the seed round, with participation from London-based PROfounders Capital.

Jordi Vidal , Partner at Kibo Ventures, commented, “We invested in Fermat because it’s the emerging category leader in AI-native fashion design, with rare early proof: explosive growth, near-zero customer churn, and tier-1 brands like New Look, J.Crew Group, and ASOS adopting it bottom-up, designer by designer.
To begin, Fermat is launching Techpacks, a tool which turns designs into factory-ready specifications.

articles.title: Finnish healthtech Treat raises €3M to tackle inefficiencies in private healthcare
Swappie co-founder’s AI HealthTech startup Treat raises €3 million to streamline private healthcare

brief.essentiel: Treat , a Helsinki-based HealthTech startup co-founded by Swappie co-founder Sami Marttinen, has raised €3 million in a pre-Seed funding round.
points: Healthtech company Treat has raised a €3 million pre-seed round led by early Lovable backer byFounders and Supercell founder Ilkka Paananen’s Illusian .
Treat connects patients in minutes with doctors who are already briefed on their medical background, eliminating unnecessary appointments and misaligned incentives in private care.
Why private healthcare profits from inefficiency Private healthcare is built on volume: clinics profit from the number of appointments and follow-ups.
The system leaves doctors with no time to review medical histories and patients caught in diagnostic ping-pong.

articles.title: UK employee benefits unicorn Stream targets IPO in 18 months

brief.essentiel: Stream , the London fintech that provides low-income employees with a range of financial services, including early access to earned wages and savings, is considering an IPO in 18 months, with London a "good possibility", its boss says.
points: The startup has raised over £170m in funding and is valued as a unicorn, according to its CEO and co-founder Peter Briffett, who is a serial entrepreneur.

Stream, which operates under a legally binding charter to “do good”, provides financial services for employees at the likes of ASDA and Next, as well as supporting 900,000 NHS staff, giving them early access to their wages.
It reported annual revenues of £67m in its latest financial figures, up 88 per cent on the year.
Its investors include QED, Smash Capital and Balderton.

articles.title: NABU secures €1.1M to bring AI automation to financial compliance

brief.essentiel: Ghent-based regtech startup NABU , which uses AI agents to automate customer due diligence (KYC) and anti-money laundering (AML) checks for regulated businesses, has raised €1.1 million in funding from a group of business angels, including former CCV owner Enny van de Velden.
points: Founded in 2025 by Karel-Lodewyck Lefere (CEO), Bart Vermeulen (CRO) and Koen Handekyn (CTO), NABU develops a platform designed to simplify compliance processes for banks, payment companies, investment funds and other regulated organisations.
Customer onboarding and regulatory compliance often involve extensive documentation, manual verification and lengthy approval processes.
Businesses must collect and review identity documents, company records and financial information, while maintaining ongoing monitoring to meet regulatory requirements.
These processes can be costly and time-consuming, particularly as regulatory scrutiny increases across Europe.

articles.title: Swiss neurotech Indivi acquires Cogitat to advance AI-powered brain monitoring

brief.essentiel: Neurotech company Indivi has acquired Cogitat , an Imperial College London spin-out developing cutting-edge deep learning models that decode cognitive function from EEG brain signals.
points: Indivi is a neurotech company headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, with offices in Córdoba, Spain and Boston, Massachusetts.

Indivi combines precision measurement, advanced analytics, and scientific expertise to help biopharmaceutical sponsors design smaller early-phase trials and detect treatment effects with greater confidence.

Cogitat’s EEG foundation model, NeuroRVQ, powers brainwave decoders that are designed to work on anyone and on any device, with the goal of doing for the brain what large language models do for language.

Its multimodal platform currently includes smartphone-based motor and cognitive assessments, with work spanning Parkinson’s disease, neuromuscular diseases including facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD), multiple sclerosis, and Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.

articles.title: Can AI be secure? It depends on where it runs

brief.essentiel: by Moterra Most UK companies are already using AI.
points: Nor is it only junior staff: TrustedTech research in May found that 62% of UK senior leaders use AI tools their organisation has not approved.
Sales teams draft proposals with it, operations teams summarise contracts, and finance teams work through spreadsheets.
The tool people settle on is often Claude, because it copes with long documents, data analysis and the routine workflows they would rather hand off.
That leaves many companies with a question they cannot yet answer: where does the data go when staff use AI?

articles.title: Opinion: Maintaining the open web is central to Europe’s AI sovereignty ambitions

brief.essentiel: Europe’s ambitions for AI sovereignty depend on giving its startups the resources to succeed, innovate and compete with established companies.
points: As it stands, the EU remains heavily reliant on digital technologies developed and managed from elsewhere, raising questions about its ability to control the systems underpinning its economy.
In June this year, the European Commission unveiled its European Technological Sovereignty Package .
The Tech Sovereignty Package also aims to fast-track the implementation of the European Commission’s existing AI Continent Action Plan.
This includes the Cloud and AI Development Act, which specifically aims to support the research, development and innovation of next-generation AI technologies, including frontier AI models.

articles.title: Nomadic bags $6M to deploy self-charging drones that spot weak points in power grids

brief.essentiel: Munich-based energy technology startup Nomadic , which develops autonomous drones that monitor high-voltage power lines while charging directly from them, has raised $6 million in a seed funding round led by Foundamental .
points: The round also attracted participation from Verve Ventures, Cyan Ventures, existing investors Outlander VC and Asia2G Capital, and angel investors from the sdw alumni network.

Founded in 2024 by Andreas Moldskred (CEO) and Lauritz Weil (CTO), Nomadic develops technology designed to help electricity grid operators monitor infrastructure, improve reliability and optimise existing grid capacity.
Growing electricity demand is putting pressure on grid operators to increase capacity while maintaining reliable operations.

However, existing grid models often overlook differences in power line conditions, while traditional monitoring methods can be costly, time-consuming and difficult to implement without disrupting operations.

articles.title: Impact Unleashed: Jack Mardack on building companies that scale positive change

brief.essentiel: What if the supposed tradeoff between commercial success and positive impact was not an unavoidable reality of business, but a problem of business design?
points: That is the central argument behind Impact Unleashed: Building Companies that Scale Positive Change , the new book by Jack Mardack , co-founder of global employment platform Oyster.

Drawing on his experience building one of the few companies to achieve both unicorn status and B Corp certification, Mardack challenges a longstanding assumption in entrepreneurship: that founders must choose between commercial success and making a meaningful difference in the world.
Instead, he argues that businesses can be designed so that growth and positive impact reinforce one another.
The principle is captured in the book’s central idea: “ impact by design, not by intention.
